findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet, where it is reachable by anyone who can reach port 3306 from an allowed network path.
storage_encrypted = false means the database volumes and snapshots are stored unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot copy can read all data.

The master password is supplied via var.password in plaintext and the master username is hardcoded to the privileged 'admin' account; the password is persisted in Terraform state and is not managed by Secrets Manager or KMS-backed rotation.
Neither the instance nor the parameter group enforces SSL/TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport), so MySQL connections may be made in cleartext, allowing credential and data interception.

The EC2 user_data script interpolates the DB master username and password directly into the instance metadata. User data is retrievable by anyone with access to the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the web app) and is stored in plaintext in Terraform state.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 is available; combined with the credential-bearing user_data and an attached instance profile, an SSRF in the PHP app yields role credentials and the DB password.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption configuration is specified, so the instance volume (which holds the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", letting a compromised web server read or destroy any S3 bucket, launch or terminate any EC2 instance, and modify or snapshot any RDS database in the account.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.
Port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group, so any workload in the VPC can attempt to reach the database directly.
skip_final_snapshot = true combined with backup_retention_period = 0 means data is irrecoverable after deletion, which an attacker with rds:* (granted above) can exploit for destructive impact.
